{{Short description|British-Polish geologist}}
[[File:The 33rd First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony.webm|thumb|thumbtime=11:56|Jan Zalasiewicz (down right) in 2023]]
'''Jan Zalasiewicz''' (born 1954 in [[Manchester]]<ref>[https://zkm.de/en/person/jan-zalasiewicz Jan Zalasiewicz] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123182700/https://zkm.de/en/person/jan-zalasiewicz |date=2023-11-23 }}.</ref>) is a British-Polish [[geologist]] and [[palaeontologist]],<ref>[https://theconversation.com/profiles/jan-zalasiewicz-153171 The Conversation Profile].</ref> emeritus professor at the [[University of Leicester]],<ref>[https://le.ac.uk/gge/people/emeritus-honorary University of Leicester staff page].</ref><ref>{{Citation | url=https://academicminute.org/2016/08/jan-zalasiewicz-university-of-leicester-a-new-age/ | title=Jan Zalasiewicz, University of Leicester - A New Age - The Academic Minute | date=5 August 2016 | publisher=academicminute.org | language=en | access-date=2020-07-09 | archive-date=2024-01-07 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240107212521/https://academicminute.org/2016/08/jan-zalasiewicz-university-of-leicester-a-new-age/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> and [[Ig Nobel]] laureate.<ref>{{Citation| title = Past Ig Winners |date =  August 2006|access-date = 2023-09-17 |publisher = improbable.com |url = https://improbable.com/ig/winners/?amp=1#ig2023| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20230917133621/https://improbable.com/ig/winners/?amp=1#ig2023 |archive-date = 2023-09-17 |language = en-US}}</ref>

== Life ==
His parents escaped from [[Siberia]] with the [[Anders' Army]].<ref>[http://wyborcza.pl/magazyn/7,124059,22839876,wiec-chodz-zafoliuj-mi-swiat-antropocen-era-czlowieka-era.html ''Więc chodź, zafoliuj mi świat. Antropocen, epoka człowieka, epoka plastiku''].</ref> He was the head of the [[Anthropocene Working Group]] from 2009 to 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthropocene Curriculum |url=https://www.anthropocene-curriculum.org/contribution/conversation-with-jan-zalasiewicz |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=www.anthropocene-curriculum.org}}</ref> In 2014, a paper co-authored by Zalasiewicz coined the term [[technofossil]].<ref name=":1">{{cite journal |last1=Zalasiewicz |first1=Jan |last2=Williams |first2=Mark |last3=Waters |first3=Colin N |last4=Barnosky |first4=Anthony D |last5=Haff |first5=Peter |date=2014-01-07 |title=The technofossil record of humans |url=https://doi.org/10.1177/2053019613514953 |journal=The Anthropocene Review |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=34–43 |doi=10.1177/2053019613514953 |hdl=2381/38871 |issn=2053-0196 |hdl-access=free}}</ref>

== Publications ==
* The Earth After Us (2008), {{ISBN|9780199214976}}.
* The Planet in a Pebble: A Journey Into Earth's Deep History (2012)
* The Cosmic Oasis: The Remarkable Story of Earth's Biosphere (2022), with Mark Williams  {{ISBN|9780198845874}}
